easy.question: Which group of food gives our body the energy to walk, run and play?
easy.explanation: Energy-giving foods like rice, roti, potato and banana are the fuels that power our body through daily activities.

easy.question: Dal, milk, paneer and eggs are examples of ______-building foods.
easy.explanation: Body-building foods help your body grow new cells, build muscles and repair injuries. They act like tiny construction workers inside you.

easy.question: Which of these is a protective food?
easy.explanation: Protective foods like spinach, carrot, orange and guava guard the body against infections and diseases, keeping skin, eyes and organs healthy.

easy.question: Why should we eat different types of food every day instead of the same food?
easy.answer: No single food item has everything our body needs. Our body requires energy from grains, building material from dal and milk, and protection from fruits and vegetables. Eating a variety of foods from all three groups keeps us healthy, strong and able to fight diseases.
easy.explanation: A balanced diet is like a three-legged stool -- all three food groups are needed for the body to function properly.

easy.question: According to Ayurveda, how many tastes (Shad Rasa) should a balanced meal include?
easy.explanation: Ayurveda identifies six tastes -- sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter and astringent -- and suggests that a complete meal should include all of them.

medium.question: Name the three groups of food and give two examples of each group.
medium.answer: 1. Energy-giving foods give us power to work and play -- examples: rice, potato. 2. Body-building foods help our body grow and get stronger -- examples: dal, milk. 3. Protective foods guard us against diseases -- examples: orange, spinach.
medium.explanation: Every food we eat belongs to one of these three groups. Eating from all three groups daily ensures our body gets a complete range of nutrients.

medium.question: Ugadi Pachadi, a dish that contains all six Ayurvedic tastes, is made during the Ugadi festival in which states?
medium.explanation: Ugadi Pachadi is prepared during the Ugadi new year celebration. It mixes jaggery, raw mango, salt, pepper, neem flowers and raw banana to represent all six tastes.

medium.question: A balanced thali should have the largest share of sabzi, salad and ______.
medium.explanation: On a balanced plate, protective foods like vegetables, salads and fruits should occupy the biggest portion, followed by body-building foods and then energy-giving foods.

hard.question: Neha eats only plain rice and roti for lunch every day. Is this a balanced meal? What should she add to her plate and why?
hard.answer: No, this is not a balanced meal. Rice and roti are only energy-giving foods. Neha is missing body-building foods and protective foods. She should add dal, paneer or dahi (body-building foods) so her body can grow and build strong muscles. She should also add vegetables like palak or gajar and a fruit like an orange or guava (protective foods) to help her body fight diseases and keep her eyes and skin healthy. A balanced meal needs food from all three groups working together.
hard.explanation: Eating from only one food group is like having a one-legged stool -- it will not support you properly. All three groups are necessary for a healthy body.

easy.question: Which of these is a nutrient-rich grain also called a super food?
easy.explanation: Millets like bajra, jowar and ragi are called super foods because they are packed with iron, calcium and fibre that keep the body healthy.

easy.question: Junk food is high in oil, salt and sugar but very low in ______.
easy.explanation: Junk food like chips, cold drinks and burgers may taste appealing but they provide almost no real nutrition to the body.

easy.question: Which of these is a junk food?
easy.explanation: Chips are loaded with excess salt and oil, and cold drinks can contain as much as ten spoons of sugar per bottle. Both are junk foods with very low nutritional value.

easy.question: Name two important things water does for our body.
easy.answer: Water helps our stomach digest food properly, and it flushes waste out of our body through urine and sweat.
easy.explanation: Water is essential for many body functions. Even though it does not give energy or build muscles, our body cannot work without it.

medium.question: What three things should you always check on the label of a packaged food item?
medium.answer: 1. Expiry date -- never eat food that has passed its expiry date as it may have gone bad. 2. Ingredients list -- the first ingredient listed is what the product contains the most of. 3. Net weight -- tells you how many grams of food are actually inside the packet.
medium.explanation: Reading food labels helps you make safe and smart choices. Checking these three things takes just a few seconds but can protect your health.

medium.question: What is a solar cooker?
options: A cooker that uses sunlight to heat food
A cooker that runs on batteries
medium.answer: A cooker that uses sunlight to heat food
medium.explanation: A solar cooker is a box with a glass lid and reflective mirrors that trap the Sun's heat to cook food. It needs no gas or electricity and produces no smoke.

hard.question: Your friend Kabir eats pizza, chips and cola for lunch every day. What advice would you give him? Explain why junk food is harmful and suggest healthier alternatives.
hard.answer: I would tell Kabir that eating junk food daily is harmful because it is packed with excess oil, sugar and salt but has very little nutrition. Chips are fried in oil heated over and over, which makes the oil dangerous. Cola can have ten spoons of sugar in one bottle, which is terrible for teeth and energy levels. Over time, this diet can make him feel tired, gain unhealthy weight and fall sick often. Instead, he should try fresh, home-cooked meals like dal-chawal, roti-sabzi or a bowl of dalia. For drinks, nimbu paani or buttermilk are refreshing and healthy. A balanced meal with foods from all three groups will keep him active and strong.
hard.explanation: Junk food gives a quick taste thrill but starves the body of real nutrition. Switching to home-cooked food is one of the best health decisions anyone can make.

easy.question: How is an idli cooked?
easy.explanation: Idlis are placed in moulds inside a steamer. The hot steam from boiling water cooks them gently without any oil.

easy.question: Jowar, bajra and ragi are types of healthy grains known as ______.
easy.explanation: Millets are small but nutrient-rich grains packed with iron, calcium and fibre. They are considered super foods in modern nutrition.

easy.question: Which of these foods needs no cooking at all?
easy.explanation: Fruit chaat is made by simply cutting and mixing fresh fruits together. No heat or cooking is needed, and it is a very healthy snack.

easy.question: Name two Indian dishes that are prepared by frying.
easy.answer: Puri and samosa are both prepared by frying in hot oil.
easy.explanation: Frying involves cooking food by dipping it in very hot oil. While tasty, fried foods should be eaten in moderation because they are high in fat.

medium.question: Why are millets called super foods? Name two examples of millets.
medium.answer: Millets are called super foods because they are packed with nutrients like iron, calcium and fibre, which keep blood healthy, bones strong and digestion smooth. Two examples are jowar (sorghum) and ragi (finger millet).
medium.explanation: Our grandparents ate millets regularly as their staple food. Today, nutritionists recommend millets as healthier alternatives to polished rice and refined wheat.

medium.question: Which cooking method is generally considered the healthiest?
medium.explanation: Steaming cooks food using hot steam without any oil or fat. This preserves the food's natural nutrients, making it one of the healthiest cooking methods.

hard.question: Name four different methods of cooking and give one example dish for each. Which method do you think is the healthiest, and why?
hard.answer: Four cooking methods are: 1. Steaming -- Idli is cooked using hot steam without oil. 2. Boiling -- Khichdi is cooked by boiling rice and dal together in water. 3. Frying -- Samosa is deep-fried in hot oil. 4. Roasting -- Bhutta (corn on the cob) is roasted over a flame or hot coals. Steaming is the healthiest method because the food is cooked gently without any oil or fat. The nutrients in the food stay intact and there is no extra grease. Fried foods taste crispy but are high in fat and should be eaten only occasionally.
hard.explanation: How food is cooked changes its nutrition value. Steaming and boiling use little or no oil, keeping food healthy. Frying adds fat and can make food less nutritious.
